blockers: Changing AGOA's eligibility rules or term requires an act of Congress; the extensions so far were short and attached to appropriations vehicles.
USTR's recommendations on modernization had not been published in the sources found.
confidence_reason: The 2028 extension was read in the text of Public Law 119-103 in an earlier review, and for this review GovInfo BILLSTATUS for H.R. 6500 (enactment and votes) and the 2026-09-18 CITA notice applying Section 2008 through 2028-12-31 were read directly. Public Law 119-75's AGOA text was not read, and whether existing eligibility criteria amount to the Mandate's strategic framework is a judgment.

durability.why: The extension is in statute (Public Laws 119-75 and 119-103), which the executive branch cannot undo, though the program sunsets at the end of 2028 and has been extended in short increments.

est_completion.basis: Inference: the extension in law runs through 2028, and any reform of the eligibility framework would most likely be taken up in the next reauthorization before the end of 2028.

proposal: The Mandate says the next Administration should extend the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which gives eligible African countries duty-free access to US markets, beyond its 2025 expiration, but within a strategic framework that rewards good governance and pro-market economic policies rather than channeling benefits to governments that fail to reform.

evidence.note: Approved 2026-09-02; Section 2008 changes the 2026 dates in Trade Act section 506B and AGOA sections 112(g), 112(b)(3) and 112(c)(1) to 2028 and sets the apparel program through 2028-12-31; it is not tied to the 2026-12-11 availability limit that governs the Act's continuing appropriations, and adds no eligibility conditions.

status_summary: AGOA's prior authorization expired on 2025-09-30. Public Law 119-75 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, enacted 2026-02-03) reauthorized it through 2026-12-31 retroactive to the expiration, and Proclamation 11030 (signed 2026-05-19) implemented the extension and designated Gabon as a beneficiary effective 2026-01-01. Public Law 119-103 (H.R. 6500, which passed the House as the AGOA Extension Act 340-54 on 2026-01-12 and the Senate 90-6 on 2026-08-08) became law on 2026-09-02; its Section 2008 moves AGOA dates from 2026 to 2028, and a CITA notice of 2026-09-18 sets apparel limits for 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30 and describes preferential treatment as running through 2028-12-31. USTR requested comments on modernizing AGOA on 2026-04-29 and began the 2027 country eligibility review on 2026-06-30, but no legislation changing eligibility, graduation or reciprocity criteria and no 2027 eligibility determinations were found as of 2026-10-21, so the extension is in law while the strategic-framework element remains at the recommendation stage.

timeline.event: AGOA's prior authorization expires, according to USTR's later notice.

The House passes H.R. 6500, introduced on 2025-12-09 as a bill to extend AGOA (passed under the title AGOA Extension Act, reported by Ways and Means on 2025-12-30), 340-54 (Roll no. 14) under suspension of the rules; the bill later became the vehicle for Public Law 119-103.

Public Law 119-75 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, H.R. 7148) is enacted; the GovInfo public law page dates it 2026-02-03. USTR's 2026-04-29 notice (below) describes it as reauthorizing AGOA through 2026-12-31, retroactive to 2025-09-30.

USTR publishes a request for comments on modernizing AGOA to inform recommendations to Congress, covering eligibility criteria, graduation, reciprocity, critical minerals supply chains and enforcement; comments closed 2026-05-15 with 136 received.

Proclamation 11030 (published 2026-05-22) implements the AGOA extension through 2026-12-31, including the regional apparel and third-country fabric programs, and designates Gabon as a beneficiary effective 2026-01-01.

USTR opens its annual review of country eligibility for AGOA for calendar year 2027, conditioned on reauthorization, applying criteria that include a market-based economy, rule of law, anti-corruption systems and worker rights, with a public hearing on 2026-07-23.
The Senate passes H.R. 6500 with an amendment and an amendment to the title, 90-6 (Record Vote 228).
The House agrees to the Senate amendments to H.R. 6500, 370-48 (Roll no. 286) under suspension of the rules; the bill is presented and signed on 2026-09-02 as Public Law 119-103.

Public Law 119-103 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027) is enacted; its Section 2008 changes the 2026 dates in AGOA's termination provision, regional apparel program and third-country fabric program to 2028 and sets the apparel program's end at 2028-12-31. The text states no new eligibility conditions.

The Committee for the Implementation of Textile Agreements publishes a notice (91 FR 59114), effective 2026-10-01, setting the AGOA duty-free apparel import limit at 1,690,799,016 square meter equivalents (845,399,508 for the lesser-developed country rule) for 2026-10-01 through 2027-09-30, citing Section 5019 of Division I of Public Law 119-75 and Section 2008 of Division B of Public Law 119-103, and stating the latter extends preferential treatment through 2028-12-31.

title: Extend AGOA past 2025 within a framework that rewards good governance
uncertainties: Public Law 119-75's AGOA text was not read directly; the 2026-02-03 reauthorization and its retroactivity come from USTR's 2026-04-29 notice. Section 2008 of Public Law 119-103 was read through a fetch summary, which reported that each 2026 reference becomes 2028 and that no effective-date clause or new conditions appear; the exact statutory end date of the main provision (beyond the apparel program's 2028-12-31 end) was not confirmed. The eligibility-review notice has an internal conflict on the testimony deadline (2026-07-09 versus 2026-07-13). Congress's role in modernizing AGOA and any pending reform bill were not searched. The Mandate does not define the strategic framework, so the match between existing eligibility criteria and the Mandate's good-governance condition is a judgment. Freshness check on 2026-10-21: GovInfo BILLSTATUS for H.R. 6500 confirms the vehicle, vote counts and enactment of Public Law 119-103 on 2026-09-02, and the 2026-09-18 CITA notice cites Section 2008 of Division B of that law and Section 5019 of Division I of Public Law 119-75 and describes preferential treatment as running through 2028-12-31, which narrows the earlier doubt on the end date for the apparel and preference program but does not quote the main termination provision. USTR's eligible-country page showed no 2027 list, and no reform bill or enacted change to the eligibility criteria was located in a web search. Public Law 119-75's own AGOA text was still not read directly.
